0.headline: From $1.3 to $74: How Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao’s equity bet could deliver nearly 5,600% gains
0.heading: From $1.3 to $74: How Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao’s equity bet could deliver nearly 5,600% gains
0.intro: According to Anthropic's latest registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on November 10, Rao beneficially owned 94.97 lakh shares as of September 30, 2026. At the proposed IPO price of $74 (around Rs 6,956) per share, the holding carries a gross notional value of approximately $703 million (around Rs 6,600 crore), assuming a dollar-rupee exchange rate of Rs 94.
0.body:
Krishna Rao, chief financial officer of artificial intelligence company Anthropic, could be sitting on shares and stock options worth nearly Rs 6,600 crore if the company's proposed initial public offering (IPO) is priced at the midpoint of its estimated price range.

According to Anthropic's latest registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on November 10, Rao beneficially owned 94.97 lakh shares as of September 30, 2026. At the proposed IPO price of $74 (around Rs 6,956) per share, the holding carries a gross notional value of approximately $703 million (around Rs 6,600 crore), assuming a dollar-rupee exchange rate of Rs 94.

However, this is not his realised wealth. The holding includes stock options that are exercisable within 60 days of September 30, 2026, and the calculation does not account for the cost of exercising them, taxes or other restrictions.

Anthropic has proposed an IPO price band of $70-78 (approximately Rs 6,580-7,332) per share and plans to list its Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT.

Rao brings nearly two decades of experience across management consulting, private equity and corporate finance. He holds a bachelor's degree in economics from Harvard College, where he graduated summa cum laude, and a Juris Doctor degree from Yale Law School.

He began his career at Bain &amp; Company in 2005, working as a strategy consultant. In 2011, he moved to Blackstone, where he worked in the private equity group, evaluating investments across consumer, retail, business services and financial technology.

His next major career move came in 2015, when he joined Airbnb. Over nearly six years at the company, he held several senior positions, including director of financial planning and analysis and global head of corporate and business development.

During his stint at Airbnb, Rao helped the company navigate the COVID-19 pandemic and played a key role in raising more than $10 billion (around Rs 94,000 crore) in equity and debt capital, including its December 2020 IPO.

He subsequently became CFO of healthcare technology company Cedar in 2021 and later served as CFO of Fanatics Commerce before joining Anthropic in April 2024.

Krishna Rao joined Anthropic as its first chief financial officer in April 2024. His offer letter, dated March 2, 2024, provided for stock options to purchase 1.4 crore shares of the company's Class A common stock under its 2021 Stock Plan.

The options carried an exercise price of just $1.30 (around Rs 122) per share. They were subject to a four-year vesting schedule, with one-fourth becoming eligible to vest after the first year and the remaining options vesting in equal monthly instalments over the following three years.

The SEC filing's year-end 2025 disclosures showed that 57.56 lakh options were exercisable, while another 81.66 lakh remained unexercisable at that point.

The latest beneficial ownership disclosure includes 1.54 lakh shares held directly by Rao, 78.43 lakh shares through options exercisable within 60 days, and another 15 lakh options held through a trust over which he exercises investment or voting control.

Rao's compensation has increased alongside his responsibilities. His annual base salary was $700,000 (around Rs 6.58 crore) in 2025. It was raised to $1.25 million (around Rs 11.75 crore) from February 1, 2026, according to the SEC filing.

The proposed IPO price is not final, and the eventual listing price could differ. Consequently, the estimated Rs 6,600-crore value of Rao's holding remains indicative rather than an amount he has already earned.

1.headline: IPO market takes a breather in November after record fundraising in September, October
1.heading: IPO market takes a breather in November after record fundraising in September, October
1.intro: India's primary IPO market slowed in November due to the festive season and Jio Platforms' record breaking issue.
1.body:
The primary market pipeline has slowed in November after blockbuster fundraising in September and October; no IPOs have opened for subscription so far this month as the festive season and overhang from the Jio Platforms IPO weighed.

However, investment bankers expect activity to pick up in the coming weeks, with a few IPOs, including Crystal Crop Protection, slated to hit the markets later this month.

In September, 34 companies hitting the market raised a total of Rs 39,381 crore. This sum was outpaced in October, with the total fundraising by 13 companies through primary markets touching Rs 44,506 crore.

A large portion of the fundraise in October was contributed to by the Jio Platforms IPO, which boasted of a Rs 30,188 crore issue size. For September, the IPO of the National Stock Exchange contributed Rs 22,563 to the total sum raised.

According to Uday Patil, Executive Director, Prabhudas Lilladher Capital Markets, the festive season was among the key reasons that IPOs have gotten delayed. "Meetings are getting postponed and people aren't available," he said, explaining why issuers are avoiding the markets at the moment. "Nothing is wrong with sentiment, it is very much intact."

Patil also added that there was a large overhang from the Jio Platforms IPO, which was India's largest. Many companies didn't want their issue to clash with the telecom giant's bid as liquidity was likely to only go towards Jio Platforms.

Now, with the overhang of Jio Platforms' IPO and the festive season completed, there is likely to be a pick-up in primary market activity. So far, only one firm: Crystal Crop Protection, has plans to tap the primary market, with the issue opening for subscription on November 18. The issue size is likely to be around Rs 550 crore.

Going forward, the IPO market may see a lull in activity towards the end of the year as the festive season will weigh once again. Foreign institutional investors are likely to be inactive during the time as they close their books for the year.

123 companies have received SEBI's approval for an issue in the past 12 months and are waiting for a better launch window, which according to a banker who did not want to be named, will occur next year, before March 31, 2026.

However, the pace of IPO launches will also depend on market conditions and the ability of companies to command the valuations they are seeking. While investor appetite remains healthy, bankers are closely watching the secondary market movements and institutional demand before they advise issuers on the timing of their offerings.

Any continued improvement in the current market sentiment will encourage more companies to go ahead with their listing plans, while any volatility could push some launches into the next financial year.

For now, bankers are of the opinion that the ongoing pause is mostly seasonal. It is not a reflection of weakening investor appetite, as the underlying pipeline remains intact.

2.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Coal India to divest up to 10% stake; here's everything you should know
2.heading: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Coal India to divest up to 10% stake; here's everything you should know
2.intro: Coal India to divest up to 10 percent stake in Mahanadi Coalfields through the proposed IPO.
2.body:
Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its initial public offering (IPO). The proposed public issue will comprise an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 66.18 crore equity shares by Coal India, according to the company's draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).

Coal India to divest up to 10 percent stake in Mahanadi Coalfields through the proposed IPO. The issue will be conducted through the book-building route, with the company's equity shares proposed to be listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSE.

SEBI issued its final observations on the draft offer document on November 4, clearing the way for the company to proceed with preparations for the public issue. However, the IPO opening date, closing date and price band have not yet been announced.

Here is a look at the key details of the proposed Mahanadi Coalfields IPO, including its issue structure, business operations, financial performance and other important disclosures.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Issue size and structure

The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 66,18,36,300 equity shares, each having a face value of Rs 2. The shares will be sold by the promoter, Coal India Limited.

Since the issue comprises only an OFS, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the IPO. The entire amount raised through the share sale will go to Coal India.

The company has proposed to reserve not more than 50 percent of the net offer for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), while not less than 15 percent will be allocated to non-institutional investors (NIIs). Retail individual investors will be eligible for at least 35 percent of the net offer.

The IPO will be managed by SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets &amp; Securities and IIFL Capital Services. KFin Technologies has been appointed as the registrar to the issue.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Important dates and price band

Mahanadi Coalfields has received SEBI's final observations on its draft offer document. However, the company has not yet announced the IPO opening and closing dates, price band, lot size or listing date.

The issue size in rupee terms will also depend on the final offer price. The DRHP specifies the number of shares proposed to be sold but does not provide a final issue value.

Mahanadi Coalfields financial performance

Mahanadi Coalfields reported revenue from operations of Rs 30,549.59 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 31,353.02 crore in FY25 and Rs 31,634.35 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements in the DRHP.

The company's revenue from operations declined 2.56 percent year-on-year in FY26.

Its profit after tax (PAT) also declined to Rs 10,698.12 crore in FY26 from Rs 10,825.12 crore in FY25. In FY24, the company had reported a PAT of Rs 11,841.55 crore.

For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Mahanadi Coalfields reported revenue from operations of Rs 8,033.77 crore, compared with Rs 7,548.37 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

However, its profit after tax declined to Rs 2,398.78 crore in the June 2026 quarter from Rs 2,448.33 crore in the June 2025 period.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Book-running lead managers and registrar

SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets &amp; Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers for the proposed IPO.

KFin Technologies has been appointed as the registrar to the issue. The equity shares are proposed to be listed on NSE and BSE.

About Mahanadi Coalfields

Incorporated on April 3, 1992, Mahanadi Coalfields is engaged in the mining and production of non-coking coal. The company was carved out of South Eastern Coalfields Limited to accelerate coal production from Odisha's Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields.

MCL is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India and holds Miniratna Category I status, which it received in December 2019.

According to the CRISIL report cited in its DRHP, Mahanadi Coalfields produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for approximately 22.40 percent of India's total non-coking coal production. It contributed around 28.3 percent of Coal India's total coal production during the same financial year.

As of June 30, 2026, the company operated 17 mines, comprising 14 opencast mines and three underground mines. Its operations are supported by coal handling plants, rapid loading systems, silos and railway connectivity.

MCL supplies different grades of non-coking coal, including washed and beneficiated coal, to power utilities, independent power producers, captive power plants and industries such as cement and sponge iron.

Note: The IPO dates, price band, lot size and final issue value are yet to be announced. The details above are based on the company's DRHP and subsequent SEBI approval.
